description:
compiler2 can compare two artifacts only by raw struct equality, which means raw
`Ty` ids. That is sound for ONE narrow case -- two compiles of the same input,
same binary, one process (see
`compiling_the_same_root_twice_publishes_byte_identical_backend_programs`). It is
the wrong comparand for anything durable.

A `Ty` is an arena index in one `World`. Across two worlds it carries no meaning:
one extra incidental intern anywhere shifts every later id without changing what
the program means.

CONSOLIDATES fz-kdt.6 (backend dump run-to-run order instability) and supplies
the cross-run comparison oracle fz-kdt.34 needs. One primitive, three consumers.

## The choice this ticket makes

Making every structure's iteration order deterministic is one way to get
comparable runs. It is unbounded work: every new `HashMap` iteration can
reintroduce the wobble, and each compensating sort is a barrier that costs real
work at runtime.

A canonical external form is bounded. Written once, id instability stops
mattering because nothing ever compares ids. The form exists ONLY for
comparison, so it lives at the sink/test boundary, never in a production path.

## Measured: `Ty` ids are not run-stable, and that is fine

`00420_enum_take_drop_split`, release, 4 separate processes, arena dumped as
(id, display) for all 1,424 slots: four different arenas, identical length,
exactly 16 differing lines in four clusters -- address vars (`a1_v0`/`a1_v1`),
two `{:cont,A}|{:cont,B}` vs `A|B` mint-order clusters, and one canonicalization
cluster (see fz-kdt.48). Program output, and the whole public work SEQUENCE,
were byte-identical across those same runs.

So the artifact means the same thing every run; only the bookkeeping is
renumbered. That is exactly what a canonical form is for.

## `Types::display` CANNOT be the type rendering

The previous version of this ticket specified "types by their canonical
`Types::display` rendering". That is measured wrong, and it is the dangerous
direction of wrong.

`display` is not injective. Same fixture, probing the compiler's own
`is_subtype` in both directions over every same-display id pair:

- `Ty(83)` and `Ty(253)` both render `([int]) -> r0`, but `253 <: 83` strictly --
  two DIFFERENT types, one string;
- `any` renders for `Ty(0)`, `Ty(82)` and `Ty(1423)`, and 82 vs 1423 are not
  comparable in either direction;
- 33 of 1,424 slots share a display with another slot; only 2 of those pairs are
  genuinely equivalent.

Rendering through `display` would make two inequivalent programs compare EQUAL.
For an equivalence oracle or a build-cache key, a false equivalence is far worse
than a false difference. The type rendering must be FAITHFUL: injective up to
type equivalence.

## Why `{:?}` also cannot be the canonical form

Measured while closing fz-f98.19: substituting every `Ty(n)` with its display
rendering in the Debug text still leaves two renderings differing at 1,703,778
characters each, first difference

    value_demands: {ValueId(70): ...   vs   value_demands: {ValueId(11): ...

`HashMap`'s Debug order is per-instance `RandomState` order, so the RENDERING is
unstable even when the structs are equal. A canonical form has to be built, not
derived from Debug.

## What is wanted

1. `canon(Ty) -> bytes`: a faithful, id-free, ordered structural rendering of a
   type. Faithful means `canon(a) == canon(b)` iff `a` and `b` are equivalent.
2. `canon(BackendProgram) -> bytes`: built on (1), maps emitted in deterministic
   key order, everything else by structure, no interned id anywhere.

Then:

- artifact EQUIVALENCE (do two builds mean the same thing?) is that form's bytes,
  surviving renumbering, cross-process and cross-version;
- artifact IDENTITY (is this the same build?) is a hash of it -- what a compile
  cache or distributed build keys on;
- a failure diff becomes legible (closing fz-f98.19 needed a throwaway Python
  multiset differ because a 1.5MB struct inequality names nothing);
- fz-kdt.34 compares work multisets across runs without needing id determinism;
- `--dump backend` becomes byte-stable (the whole of fz-kdt.6).

## Bonus: it is the ratchet for interner canonicalization

With a faithful `canon`, `canon(a) == canon(b) && a != b` is exactly "one type,
two identities" -- a one-line permanent guard. That is the defect fz-kdt.48
records, and this ticket supplies its regression ratchet (fz-kdt.48 does not
depend on this ticket to be FIXED, only to be permanently guarded).

## Where it lives

Comparison-only. Emit sites pass the raw `Ty` plus the owning authority
(`&World`/`&Types`); the handler or test computes the external form. A
telemetry-disabled run must render nothing. Memoize by `Ty` in the handler: a
compile has ~1,424 distinct types against ~17,500 events, so the cost is per
distinct type, not per event.

## Not the answer

A global after-the-fact renumbering pass over the interner arena. It is a barrier
needing the whole arena, it invalidates `Ty` as a stable handle for every memo
keyed by it, and it would leave the work order nondeterministic while making only
the ids look stable.

Nor is it "make every structure deterministic" -- see The choice above.

## Both existing tests stay

fz-f98.19's defect (the same 836 types minted in a permuted order) is INVISIBLE
under canonicalization, because every position renders the same. That is the
point, not a gap: canonical form measures the artifact, raw ids measure the
bookkeeping, and the job-order test measures the cause. Adding this must not
delete either existing test, and the docs must say which property each measures.

## Checks

- `canon(Ty)` is faithful: a test asserts `canon(a) == canon(b)` iff mutually
  subtype, over the full arena of both target fixtures.
- A canonical rendering exists for `BackendProgram` with no interned id in it,
  stable across two in-process compiles by construction (no sort of Debug text).
- Two SEPARATE PROCESSES produce the identical canonical form for one input.
- `--dump backend` is byte-identical across repeated runs (absorbs fz-kdt.6).
- The existing raw-equality and job-order tests still pass, documented as
  measuring different properties.
- `dump.rs`'s existing render_* helpers are reused or folded in rather than
  duplicated -- check before writing a second renderer.
title: Canonical external form: one faithful, id-free rendering for Ty and BackendProgram
